name: Bagalkote
summary: Historic district famed for Badami cave temples, Pattadakal UNESCO monuments, and Ilkal sarees.

profile.Crafts: Ilkal sarees, Guledgudda Khana fabrics

points: Cradle of early Chalukyan rock-cut architecture at Badami, Aihole, and Pattadakal
Prominent center of North Karnataka handloom textile clusters

name: Ballari
summary: Mining and industrial hub known for historic Ballari Fort atop the massive monolithic rock.

profile.Crafts: Jeans apparel manufacturing

points: Ballari Fort built by Hanumappa Nayaka and later fortified by French engineers for Hyder Ali
Major center of iron ore mining and garment production in South India

name: Belagavi
summary: Sugar capital and commercial crossroad bordering Goa and Maharashtra, famed for Belagavi Kunda.

profile.Crafts: Brass and copper utensils, Shahapur sarees

points: Second legislative capital of Karnataka hosting the winter assembly session at Suvarna Vidhana Soudha
Belagavi Fort dates back to Ratta dynasty in 1204 CE

name: Bengaluru Rural
summary: Agricultural and poultry belt surrounding the tech metropolis, home to Kempegowda International Airport.

profile.Crafts: Silk worm rearing, Handloom weaving

points: Encompasses Devanahalli Fort, the birthplace of 18th-century ruler Tipu Sultan
Major floriculture, dairy, and silk cocoon production region

name: Bengaluru Urban
summary: Silicon Valley of India, premier center for global information technology, aerospace, and startup innovation.

profile.Food: Benne Masala Dosa, Filter Coffee, Kesari Bath
profile.Crafts: Mysore silk showroom weaving, Sandalwood products

points: Founded in 1537 by chieftain Kempe Gowda I who built a mud fort
Headquarters of ISRO, Infosys, Wipro, and over 400 multinational R&D tech centers

name: Bidar
summary: Crown city of Karnataka, medieval capital of Bahmani and Barid Shahi sultanates, famed for Bidriware.

profile.Crafts: GI-tagged Bidriware silver inlay on blackened zinc alloy

points: Bidar Fort built in 1428 CE by Ahmad Shah Wali Bahmani with 30 bastions
Houses Mahmud Gawan Madrasa, 15th-century Islamic university with Persian minarets

name: Chamarajanagar
summary: Southern borderland where Western and Eastern Ghats meet, famous for Bandipur Tiger Reserve and wild silk.

profile.Crafts: Raw silk production, Bamboo craft

points: Bandipur National Park forms a key component of the Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve
Named after Chamaraja Wadiyar IX, 18th-century Maharaja of Mysore who was born here

name: Chikkaballapura
summary: Hilly terrain featuring scenic Nandi Hills, grape vineyards, and Muddenahalli, birthplace of Sir M. Visvesvaraya.

profile.Crafts: Mulberry silk cultivation, Incense agarbatti

points: Nandi Hills was summer retreat of Tipu Sultan and British administrators
Birthplace of Bharat Ratna engineer-statesman Sir M. Visvesvaraya in Muddenahalli

name: Chikkamagaluru
summary: Cradle of Indian coffee nestled in the Western Ghats under Mullayanagiri, Karnataka's highest peak.

profile.Crafts: Coffee processing, Wood carving

points: Sufi saint Baba Budan smuggled seven raw coffee beans from Yemen and planted them here in 1670 CE
Mullayanagiri peak rises to 1,930 m above sea level

name: Chitradurga
summary: Historic granite fortress city celebrated for the seven-walled Chitradurga Fort and heroic legend of Onake Obavva.

profile.Crafts: Cotton ginning, Stone masonry

points: Chitradurga Fort (Kallina Kote) built by Nayaka palegars features seven concentric fortification walls
Legendary heroine Onake Obavva single-handedly defended a secret passage against invading troops

name: Dakshina Kannada
summary: Coastal economic capital centered at Mangaluru, cradle of Indian private banking, Yakshagana, and coastal seafood.

profile.Food: Neer Dosa, Kori Rotti, Mangalore Buns, Ghee Roast
profile.Crafts: Cashew nut processing, Coastal boat building

points: New Mangalore Port is Karnataka's only major sea port handling maritime container cargo
Birthplace of major Indian commercial banks including Canara Bank, Syndicate Bank, and Corporation Bank

name: Davanagere
summary: The Manchester of Karnataka, renowned for historical cotton spinning mills and crisp Davanagere Benne Dosa.

profile.Crafts: Cotton textile weaving, Sugar processing

points: Flourished under Haider Ali and became a premier cotton textile and trading mart on the Tungabhadra River
Famous for GI-tagged Davanagere Benne Dosa prepared on firewood iron griddles

name: Dharwad
summary: Cultural hub of Hindustani classical music, literary capital of Kannada Renaissance, and home to Dharwad Peda.

profile.Crafts: Kasuti traditional embroidery, Navalur handloom

points: Nurtured musical giants: Mallikarjun Mansur, Bhimsen Joshi, and Gangubai Hangal
GI-tagged Dharwad Peda crafted from caramelized Dharwadi buffalo milk since the 19th century

name: Gadag
summary: Heart of Western Chalukya temple architecture, home to the historic Veeranarayana Temple and printing presses.

profile.Crafts: Handloom weaving of Betageri, Wind turbine generation

points: Kalyani Chalukyas developed the distinctive Gadag architectural style in 11th–12th century temples
Poet Kumaravyasa composed the monumental Kannada Mahabharata (Gadugina Bharata) inside Veeranarayana Temple

name: Hassan
summary: Architectural wonderland of Hoysala temples at Belur and Halebidu, and colossal monolithic Gommateshwara.

profile.Crafts: Soapstone stone carving, Coffee processing

points: Hoysala sacred ensembles at Belur and Halebidu inscribed on UNESCO World Heritage list in 2023
Shravanabelagola features 57-foot Gommateshwara monolith erected in 981 CE by Ganga minister Chavundaraya

name: Haveri
summary: Agricultural hub celebrated for fiery red Byadagi chillies, cardamoms, and historic Chalukyan shrines.

profile.Food: Byadagi chilli spiced gravies, Jolada Rotti
profile.Crafts: Byadagi chilli spice trading, Cardamom garland making

points: Byadagi chilli market is Asia's second-largest chilli market, known for deep red color and low pungency
Birthplace of famous saint-philosophers Kanakadasa (Bada) and Sarvajna (Abalur)

name: Kalaburagi
summary: Historic medieval capital of Bahmani Sultanate, center of Sufism at Khwaja Bande Nawaz Dargah, and pulse capital.

profile.Crafts: Red gram (Toor dal) processing, Shahabad limestone tiles

points: Gulbarga Fort built in 1347 CE houses the unique Jama Masjid built entirely with covered domed roofs
GI-tagged Kalaburagi Red Gram (Toor Dal) supplies major protein across southern India

name: Kodagu
summary: Scotland of India, misty highlands along the Western Ghats famed for Arabica coffee, pepper, and martial Kodava culture.

profile.Food: Pandi Curry, Kadambuttu, Akki Rotti, Bamboo Shoot fry
profile.Crafts: Coorg honey, Spices, Traditional Peeche Kathi silver daggers

points: Origin of sacred river Kaveri at Talakaveri in the Brahmagiri hills
Birthplace of Field Marshal K. M. Cariappa, first Indian Commander-in-Chief of Indian Army

name: Kolar
summary: Land of Golden Fields (KGF), silk cocoon markets, and the premier tomato wholesale trade hub of South India.

profile.Crafts: Raw silk processing, Tomato wholesale trade

points: Kolar Gold Fields (KGF) was one of the deepest and oldest gold mines in the world, operational for over a century
Someshwara Temple showcases ornate 14th-century Vijayanagara Dravidian architecture

name: Koppal
summary: Historical gateway to Vijayanagara kingdom, internationally famous for traditional Kinhal painted wooden toys.

profile.Crafts: GI-tagged Kinhal painted woodcraft, Handloom weaving

points: GI-tagged Kinhal toys crafted by Chitragar community using light wood and liquid gold foil since Vijayanagara times
Mahadeva Temple at Itagi hailed as Devalaya Chakravarti (Emperor among temples) by Western Chalukyas

name: Mandya
summary: Sugar Bowl of Karnataka on the fertile Kaveri basin, celebrated for Krishna Raja Sagara Dam and Maddur Vada.

profile.Food: Maddur Vada, Ragi Mudde with Nati Koli, Jaggery
profile.Crafts: Organic sugarcane jaggery processing

points: Irrigated by the Krishna Raja Sagara (KRS) Dam constructed under Sir M. Visvesvaraya in 1932
Historic island town of Srirangapatna served as capital of Tipu Sultan and Hyder Ali

name: Mysuru
summary: The Heritage City of palaces, royal Wadiyar dynasty, Mysore Dasara, fragrant sandalwood, and Mysore silk.

profile.Food: Mysore Pak, Mysore Masala Dosa, Mylari Dosa
profile.Crafts: Mysore silk sarees, Sandalwood carving, Rosewood inlay with ivory/acrylic

points: Mysore Palace is one of India's most visited royal palaces, illuminated by 97,000 bulbs on festivals
Dasara festival celebrated with grand Jumboo Savari elephant procession since 1610 CE

name: Raichur
summary: Doab territory between Krishna and Tungabhadra rivers, famous for Raichur Thermal Power Station and Sona Masuri rice.

profile.Food: Jolada Rotti, Sona Masuri rice delicacies
profile.Crafts: Rice milling, Cotton processing

points: Raichur Doab contested bitterly between Vijayanagara Empire and Bahmani Sultanate for its agricultural wealth
Raichur Fort features massive stone blocks fitted without mortar in 1294 CE

name: Ramanagara
summary: Silk City and Toy Town, famed for Asia's largest cocoon market, Channapatna wooden lacquer toys, and Sholay rock boulders.

profile.Food: Ragi Mudde, Maddur Vada, Masala Dosa
profile.Crafts: GI-tagged Channapatna wooden lacquer toys, Mulberry silk reeling

points: Channapatna toys craft originated under patronage of Tipu Sultan who invited Persian ivory artisans
Massive granite hillocks formed the famous cinematic setting for the film Sholay

name: Shivamogga
summary: Gateway to Malnad, rice granary of Karnataka, home to Jog Falls, Western Ghats biodiversity, and Keladi heritage.

profile.Food: Akki Rotti, Halasina Hannina Kadabu, Thambli
profile.Crafts: Areca nut products, Sandalwood carving

points: Jog Falls drops 253 m in four majestic cascades: Raja, Roarer, Rocket, and Rani
Keladi Nayakas ruled from Ikkeri and Keladi leaving remarkable stone temples in 16th–18th century

name: Tumakuru
summary: Industrial satellite and educational hub known for Siddaganga Mutt's social service, Tatte Idli, and coconut groves.

profile.Crafts: Coir fiber rope and matting, Handloom cotton

points: Siddaganga Mutt founded by Shivakumar Swamiji feeds and educates over 10,000 poor students daily
Devarayanadurga hill temples showcase Chola and Vijayanagara architecture

name: Udupi
summary: Spiritual seaside temple town on the Arabian Sea, birthplace of Dvaita Vedanta and globally renowned Udupi vegetarian cuisine.

profile.Food: Udupi Masala Dosa, Goli Baje, Patrode, Kadubu
profile.Crafts: Udupi pure cotton sarees, Temple wood carvings

points: Sri Krishna Matha founded in 13th century by philosopher Madhvacharya who established Ashta Mathas
St. Mary's Islands feature world-renowned hexagonal columnar basaltic lava rock formations

name: Uttara Kannada
summary: Dense coastal forest district boasting sacred Gokarna Atma Linga shrine, Murudeshwar beach, and Dandeli tiger reserve.

profile.Food: Karwar Fish Thali, Toddy palm jaggery, Cashews
profile.Crafts: Sandalwood carving of Kumta, Horn and shell art

points: Mahabaleshwar Temple at Gokarna houses the sacred Pranalinga (Atma Linga) of Lord Shiva
Over 75% of district area covered under dense evergreen Western Ghats forests

name: Vijayanagara
summary: Heritage heartland created in 2021 centered at Hosapete, containing the majestic UNESCO World Heritage ruins of Hampi.

profile.Crafts: Stone sculpture, Terracotta, Lambani tribal embroidery

points: Imperial capital of Vijayanagara Empire from 1336 to 1565 CE, visited by European and Persian travelers
Encompasses Virupaksha Temple, Stone Chariot at Vittala Temple, and Lotus Mahal

name: Vijayapura
summary: City of domes on the Deccan plateau, historical seat of Adil Shahi dynasty boasting Gol Gumbaz and Ibrahim Rauza.

profile.Food: Jolada Rotti, Shenga Chutney, Grapes, Pomegranate
profile.Crafts: Lambani embroidery, Ilkal border handlooms

points: Gol Gumbaz (built 1656 CE) features the world's second largest dome without pillar support and an acoustic whispering gallery
Capital of Adil Shahi Sultanate which constructed Ibrahim Rauza ('Taj Mahal of the Deccan')

name: Yadgir
summary: Hill fortress district on the Bhima River, historic seat of Western Chalukyas and Rashtrakutas, and agricultural pulse center.

profile.Crafts: Handloom weaving, Red gram processing

points: Yadgir Fort built atop a massive hill feature by Western Chalukya and Yadava dynasties
Carved out of Kalaburagi as an independent district in December 2009
